grammar.title: Possibility and probability: must / may / might / could
grammar.explanation: When you talk about how sure you are, English uses different modal verbs. Use must when you are almost 100 percent sure: it is a logical conclusion from what you see or know. Use may or might when it is 50-50: possible, but you are not sure. Use could for a weak possibility. For a negative conclusion use can't. Note: mustn't means 'not allowed', which is different. For the past, use must have plus the past participle.
examples: His father must be very proud of him.
She must be tired after the long trip.
You must be joking. That can't be true!
He must have found his keys. They are on the table.
It may rain tomorrow, so take an umbrella.
She might be at home, but I am not sure.
This old car could break down at any moment.
